outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in writing for various media platforms, including print, online, and broadcast, with an emphasis on clarity, accuracy, and journalistic style.
Develop effective interviewing techniques to gather information from diverse sources, ensuring thorough and reliable reporting.
Conduct research, critically evaluate sources, and analyze information to produce well-informed and contextually rich journalistic content.
Understand and apply ethical principles and legal considerations specific to journalism, including issues related to accuracy, fairness, privacy, and freedom of the press.

Develop skills necessary for working in a newsroom environment including deadline management, collaboration, and effective communication with editors and colleagues, and using relevant technologies, software, and tools essential for modern journalism such as content management systems, digital editing software, and social media platforms.
Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of diversity and inclusion in journalism, reflecting it in coverage and story selection to represent a broad range of perspectives.
Gain proficiency in the editing and production process, understanding how to present news stories effectively through layout, design, and multimedia elements.
Assemble a comprehensive portfolio showcasing a variety of journalistic work, demonstrating growth and competence over the duration of the certificate program.

notes: Read the Journalism Certificate of Achievement section (page 308) only; the AA-T and the Multimedia Journalism certificate are separate sections.
Total of 12 units taken from 'The Certificate of Achievement can be obtained upon completion of the 12-unit major.'
Catalog prints codes with leading zeros (JOUR 001, 011, 060, 061); treated as the closed list's JOUR 1, 11, 60, 61.

The outcomes lead-in under this certificate says 'Students who complete the Associate in Arts in Journalism for Transfer will be able to:', apparently a catalog copy error; the eight outcomes differ from the AA-T's and are recorded for this certificate.
